title: Slack Zendesk Integration: How to Connect Them Both Ways
summary: A slack zendesk integration connects your support ticketing and messaging tools to streamline ticket updates and team collaboration in real time.
body_markdown:
## Step-by-step: Building a real-time ticket alert workflow


Automation bridges the gap between customer distress and engineering response by ensuring critical data lands in the exact Slack channel where your team already operates.


This specific workflow maps incoming support requests to a notification engine that filters for urgency, preventing high-priority issues from rotting in an unread inbox.


### Step 1: Connect the Zendesk New Ticket trigger


You must authorize a connection to your Zendesk instance before the automation tool can listen for state changes. In the workflow builder, select the Zendesk trigger labeled New Ticket, which initiates the flow every time a customer submits a request.


The automation lacks the permissions required to poll your ticket queue without a Zendesk Subdomain and an API Token. Once you verify the connection, the trigger will expose a schema containing the Ticket ID, Subject, and Description.


### Filtering Zendesk tickets by priority before alerting Slack


To prevent channel noise, you must insert a logical gate between the trigger and the notification. Add a Filter step immediately after the Zendesk trigger in the builder interface.


Set the condition to check the Priority field from the Zendesk ticket data. Configure the operator to "Equals" and the value to "High" to ensure only critical incidents proceed to the next step.


By applying this filter, you ensure the #urgent-support channel remains a high-signal environment rather than a dumping ground for low-priority feature requests.


### Step 2: Format the Slack message action


Because a developer needs to assess the issue without leaving their chat interface, you must map the raw JSON output from Zendesk into a readable Slack block. Select Slack as your action app and choose the Post Message method.


Activepieces allows you to generate these specific integration steps with AI and add them privately to your own instance, bypassing the wait for vendor release cycles.


The open-source monorepo on GitHub shows **748 integrations** that form the floor of the catalogue, roughly 60% of which are community-contributed, ensuring that the majority of your tools rely on the collective activity of builders rather than a single vendor's roadmap, which means your infrastructure is shielded from the risks of **proprietary lock-in** .


Use the dynamic data pills from the previous step to include the Ticket Subject and a direct URL to the ticket in the message text field.


Providing a clickable link reduces the time-to-resolution by eliminating the need to manually search the Zendesk dashboard. You should also select the specific Slack channel, such as #ops-alerts, to ensure the notification reaches the correct on-call rotation.


### Step 3: Test the connection and go live


Validation is the final gate. It requires you to trigger a mock event in Zendesk to verify that the data payload correctly traverses the bridge and renders in Slack.


Create a test ticket in your Zendesk sandbox (an isolated environment for development) with the priority set to High to satisfy your filter criteria.


Success is the goal in the execution log. A failure here usually indicates a malformed API token or a mismatch in channel permissions. Once the test message appears in Slack with the correct formatting, toggle the workflow to Active to begin processing live customer data.
